clue.text: Lots of lucre, but little luck

parts.note: little means small
luck is fortune

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a pile of money came with only a little luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a lot of money is ironic: it calls a large sum small.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a great deal of money, said with understatement.

clue.text: Amount of time that is left for the dog

parts.note: a span is a period of time
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some time is set aside for the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog with long ears, such as the cocker.

clue.text: A strange plant

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: An odd-looking plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-like plant, cuckoo-pint, with a hooded spathe.

clue.text: The final batsman has to keep ongoing

explanation.surface: The last cricketer in has to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman not dismissed at the end of an innings is described this way; to last out also means to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: The batter dismissed last in cricket, and to survive or endure to the end.

clue.text: I'd eat no curry!

indicators.note: to curry is to cook up or mix in a spicy dish, so the letters are stirred around

explanation.surface: A slimmer refuses the takeaway curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like the food refused but rearranges I'D EAT NO; the whole clue is also what a slimmer says.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restricting food intake to lose weight would refuse rich dishes.

clue.text: Neat haircut

explanation.surface: A tidy haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and smart, and a light cut to the hair.

clue.text: Most orderly way to take food in the snuggery

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the cosy-room word

parts.note: a snuggery is a cosy nook, a nest
to take food is to eat

explanation.surface: The tidiest approach is to dine in your cosy den.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of neat, meaning tidiest.

clue.text: Has coming to grips with his opponent exhausted him?

definitions.text: Has coming to grips with his opponent exhausted him?

parts.words: Has coming to grips with his opponent exhausted him?
parts.note: a fighter who grapples freestyle, and also one left completely worn out by the bout

explanation.surface: A grappler is left drained after a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All in' means exhausted, and all-in wrestling is a freestyle form with few holds barred.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in freestyle wrestling, where almost any hold is allowed.

clue.text: Novel incident in a Thames Valley town

parts.note: Reading is a town in Berkshire on the River Thames
an incident or affair is a matter

explanation.surface: An unusual event happens in a town by the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is an example of books and print for reading.

clue.text: Outdated measures by the unions

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned measures are taken by the trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: An old measure of distance of about three miles; also associations or alliances of clubs or nations.

clue.text: Cause a stir by setting it in stone

indicators.note: setting one thing in another puts these letters inside the stone word

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jeweller makes a fuss by mounting a gem in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' suggests jewellery; the stone is AGATE with IT placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or disturb is a synonym, as in stirring public feeling.

clue.text: A bit of an eye for a girl

explanation.surface: A bit of an eye is what a girl gives?
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye, and a female first name.

clue.text: How to make bitter beer? Go away!

explanation.surface: A brewer is told to clear off after asking about bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hops give beer its bitterness, so to make bitter you would hop the brew; the phrase is also slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque British command to depart; also adding hops to a brew, as for bitter ale.

clue.text: Have an inclination to nurse

explanation.surface: Someone feels inclined to take up nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disposed or likely, and to look after someone sick.

clue.text: Study-leave in Africa

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A student takes sabbatical leave in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A country and river in central Africa.

clue.text: Provide accommodation either way

indicators.note: the letters read identically from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A host offers lodging whichever way it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To house or lodge a guest for the night.

clue.text: The strike no one takes sitting down

definitions.text: The strike no one takes sitting down

parts.words: The strike no one takes sitting down
parts.note: a strike in which workers leave on foot, so nobody stays seated, unlike a sit-in

explanation.surface: Workers mount an industrial action that nobody will tolerate passively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes sitting down' sounds like accepting meekly; literally, strikers stand and leave the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike in which employees leave their workplace in protest.

clue.text: Continue to mock a county town

parts.note: to mock is to taunt
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: Locals keep jeering at a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative centre of Somerset, a county in England.

clue.text: Sensing disarray among American naval officers

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so the letters of the word before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors pick up on confusion among the American fleet's officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior commissioned officers in the US Navy hold this rank.

clue.text: Unusually rash writer put on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue the writer is placed on, after, the scrambled letters
unusually signals the word after is to be formed in an unusual order

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An oddly reckless author is made nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on edge' reads as making nervous; 'put on' places PEN after SHAR, the rearranged RASH, and 'edge' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge a blade is to give it a keen cutting side.

clue.text: Small creditor carrying little weight

parts.note: a creditor is a lender

explanation.surface: A minor moneylender is slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim, light of build.

clue.text: Rio must be ruined by the travel industry

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the two words before are scrambled

explanation.surface: Rio de Janeiro will be spoilt by holidaymakers and the business serving them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be ruined' looks like one phrase, but 'must' is fodder: RIO plus MUST rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The business of providing holidays, hotels and sightseeing for visitors.

clue.text: The ground to soak up water from above

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: The soil absorbs the downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak up' looks like one verb; 'up' turns RET (to soak flax) into TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of land considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Longing to be cured of eczema

definitions.text: Longing to be cured of eczema

parts.words: Longing to be cured of eczema
parts.note: eager to get rid of the skin complaint, which also describes the very symptom that eczema causes

explanation.surface: A sufferer is desperate to be rid of a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both eager and the prickly sensation eczema causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Means eager or longing, and the irritation of the skin.

clue.text: Some come back for gin

indicators.note: coming back suggests returning, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: some means part

explanation.surface: A few return for a glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is a snare for animals, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is also a device for catching game, a snare.

clue.text: Listened to the Home Secretary speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the name is said out loud and a word sounding the same is taken

parts.note: Douglas Hurd was British Home Secretary from 1985 to 1989, when this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: The minister in charge of policing was listened to as he spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas Hurd was the UK's Home Secretary (interior minister) in the late 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of hear, meaning paid attention to with the ears.

clue.text: Tax a man north of the border

definitions.text: a man north of the border

explanation.surface: A levy is charged on a man in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of the border' means in Scotland, from an English viewpoint; scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: An old levy or payment, as in scot-free, and a native of Scotland.

clue.text: Compassion was what she showed her mother-in law

explanation.surface: Kindness was the trait a daughter-in-law showed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Ruth stays loyally with her mother-in-law Naomi; ruth is also an archaic word for pity.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for pity, and the biblical woman devoted to Naomi.

clue.text: Friend and I discover old Indian language

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Two people find an ancient tongue of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient language of Theravada Buddhist scriptures.

clue.text: Hold forth on former British currency

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former
the pound sterling is British money

explanation.surface: An economist lectures at length about old British money.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain or set out at length, often lecturing.

clue.text: Cupidity is a wicked habit consuming a king

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the vice word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a vice is a wicked habit
taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Greed is a sin that devours even a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity means greed for wealth, a synonym.

clue.text: Where the race is won is under consideration

explanation.surface: A punter describes where a race is decided and who is still a contender.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, the stretch where a race is contested; idiomatically, still with a chance of selection.
